source_documents.title: Aggregation-Induced Emission: Effects of Molecular Structure, Solid-State Conformation, and Morphological Packing Arrangement on Light-Emitting Behaviors of Diphenyldibenzofulvene Derivatives
A conical intersection model to explain aggregation induced emission in diphenyl dibenzofulvene

reference_evidence_units.quote: a ring-closed form of 1 with one of its phenyl blades locked, was emissive in the solutions
reference_evidence_units.subject: Ring-closed compound 3 compared with DPDBF 1
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Solution emission of a chemically locked analogue in the 2007 paper.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Locking one phenyl blade in an analogue is associated with solution emission.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Chemical locking changes the molecule; it is not a same-molecule intervention.

reference_evidence_units.quote: their intramolecular rotations are greatly restricted by the surrounding molecules
reference_evidence_units.subject: DPDBF derivatives 1 and 2
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Crystal versus solution comparison in the 2007 paper.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The earlier paper explains crystal emission through restricted phenyl rotation.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: This broad interpretation should not be treated as independent proof of the later CI pathway.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The crystals of 1 and 2 emitted stronger, bluer lights than their amorphous powders
reference_evidence_units.subject: DPDBF derivatives 1 and 2
reference_evidence_units.statement: Packing state changes emission intensity and color.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: The source's conformational explanation is separate from the observed spectral change.

reference_evidence_units.quote: In solution, the seam is accessed through rotation around the exocyclic fulvene bond, leading to radiationless decay to the ground state.
reference_evidence_units.subject: DPDBF
reference_evidence_units.conditions: 2013 multireference quantum-chemical model of solution photophysics.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The later model identifies a torsion-accessible conical-intersection decay route.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: This is a theoretical refinement of the older motion-restriction explanation.

reference_evidence_units.quote: In the solid, the seam cannot be accessed because the torsion is blocked, and DPDBF becomes emissive.
reference_evidence_units.subject: DPDBF
reference_evidence_units.statement: Crystal confinement blocks the modeled nonradiative route.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: The result is conditional on the crystal model, not all aggregates or packing forms.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The faint emission observed in experiments peaks at 441 nm (2.81 eV) and comes from this minimum
reference_evidence_units.subject: DPDBF
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Assignment to the S2-Minac minimum after approximately 350 nm excitation in acetonitrile.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The model assigns the faint solution fluorescence to S2 rather than S1.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: The S2 attribution is computationally motivated and condition-specific, not direct state-resolved experimental proof.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Time-resolved spectra for DPDBF would be interesting in this context to confirm that the excited state lifetime in solution corresponds to decay at a CI.
reference_evidence_units.subject: DPDBF
reference_evidence_units.statement: The paper identifies time-resolved confirmation of CI decay as future work.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: This sentence must not be converted into a completed ultrafast measurement.

reference_evidence_units.quote: This indicates that, in contrast to the solution case, emission in the solid comes from the S1 state.
reference_evidence_units.subject: DPDBF
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Comparison of calculated solid-state emission with experiment.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The later paper assigns different emitting states in solution and solid.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: This is a model-based assignment; preserve the source's state and wavelength uncertainties.

reference_evidence_units.quote: This disfavours exciton formation because the coupling between the DPDBF monomers is small
reference_evidence_units.subject: DPDBF
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Crystal model with nonparallel DBF slabs; the supporting TD-DFT calculations are cited in the SI.
reference_evidence_units.statement: The later paper argues that weak intermolecular coupling disfavors exciton formation in its crystal model.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: This is a model- and packing-specific argument, not a universal exclusion of excitons in all DPDBF aggregates. The cited SI calculation is not yet verified.

reference_mechanisms.label: RIM_RIR_RIV
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Retain the earlier broad motion-restriction account, explicitly linked to the later CI refinement, not an unrelated co-primary cause.

reference_mechanisms.label: PACKING_HOST_MATRIX_CONFINEMENT
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Packing provides the constraint that suppresses torsion and changes emission.

reference_mechanisms.label: RACI_CI_ACCESS
reference_mechanisms.rationale: The 2013 source gives a specific CI-access account of nonradiative decay and its restriction in the solid.

reference_mechanisms.label: SOKR_ANTI_KASHA
reference_mechanisms.rationale: The later source assigns solution emission to S2 and solid emission to S1. The higher-state assignment is conditional and theoretical.
